issues.description: Method SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery: The problem statement's UML specifies a public method '+acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int): void', while the reference implementation declares it with package-private visibility as 'static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)'. The template's Main.java also shows a call to acceptSupplyDelivery (shop.acceptSupplyDelivery(...)). This visibility mismatch can confuse students about whether the method should be implemented as public (as in the UML/spec) or package-private (as in the solution) and about the intended API accessibility from other classes/packages.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the acceptSupplyDelivery method public in the reference implementation to match the UML and the problem statement. Change the signature in SealSaloon.java to: 'public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)'. Also update the problem statement text (or UML) to explicitly state that acceptSupplyDelivery is a public static API method so students know to implement it as public static.
